Senses.Explanation: To divide (分) and to distinguish or separate (別): 'to distinguish' or 'tell apart,' and as a noun, distinguishing. The Chan corpus most often places it in negative constructions: 'do not arouse distinguishing' (不起分別), 'do not distinguish' (莫分別), and 'apart from distinguishing' (離分別). It is paired with 'thinking' (思量)—'thinking and distinguishing' (思量分別, 165 occurrences)—and with 'deluded thought' (妄想), as 'deluded-thought distinguishing' (妄想分別). Dahui says, 'this matter is not what thinking and distinguishing can grasp; now say—when you neither distinguish nor think, what is it?' (是法非思量分別之所能解。且道不分別不思量時是箇甚麼). One passage says, 'because of second-thought distinguishing there are marks; apart from distinguishing there really are no marks' (以第二念分別故有相；若離分別，實無有相). Another says, 'when the distinguishing mind arises, one sees objects existing—this is called ignorance' (分別心起，見有境界，名為無明). A positive use also occurs: the Platform Record preserves the line, 'well able to distinguish the marks of all things, yet unmoved from the first principle' (能善分別諸法相，於第一義而不動). Attested collocations include 'the distinguishing mind' (分別心, 88 occurrences), 'without distinguishing' (無分別, 436), 'arouse or not arouse distinguishing' (起／不起分別), 'thinking and distinguishing' (思量分別), and 'deluded-thought distinguishing' (妄想分別). The entry records these uses without replacing 'distinguish' with an abstract theory.
Senses.Note: The Chan-record deployment is predominantly "the distinguishing to be dropped" (不起／莫／離分別, "do not arouse / do not / apart from distinguishing," paired with "thinking" (思量) and "deluded thought" (妄想)), while the Platform Sutra preserves a positive "well able to distinguish the marks of all things" (善分別諸法相). The Records of the Source-Mirror (宗鏡錄) witness by Yongming Yanshou (永明延壽) comes from expository prose and supplies the explicit equation that the arising of the distinguishing mind (分別心) is called ignorance (無明). Compare "thinking" (思量), "deluded thought" (妄想), and "the distinguishing mind" (分別心).

Occurrences.Kwic: 能善分別諸法相，於第一義而不動。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Platform Sutra of the Sixth Ancestor's Teaching Treasure (Platform Sutra of the Sixth Ancestor's Teaching Treasure (Platform Sutra of the Sixth Ancestor's Teaching Treasure (六祖大師法寶壇經))); a Vimalakīrti-sūtra line quoted approvingly (故經云…, "therefore the sutra says…") — the preserved positive sense: skillful distinguishing that does not disturb the first principle. Raised sutra quote, MasterName null.

Occurrences.Kwic: 是法非思量分別之所能解。且道不分別不思量時是箇甚麼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄), by Dahui Zonggao, his upper-hall address (上堂) — he abruptly takes the staff and strikes it down once (驀拈拄杖卓一下), then says this; distinguishing (分別) paired with thinking (思量) as what cannot reach "this matter" (是法).

Occurrences.Kwic: 以第二念分別故有相；若離分別
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Teaching Altar of Chan Master Shiyu (石雨禪師法檀), the record of Shiyu Mingfang (石雨明方), in an address to the assembly (示眾). The passage says that marks arise with second-thought distinguishing and are absent apart from it (分別). Shiyu Mingfang is absent from the roster, so MasterName is null.

Occurrences.Kwic: 分別心起。見有境界。名為無明。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Records of the Source-Mirror (宗鏡錄), by Yongming Yanshou (永明延壽). The passage equates the arising of the distinguishing mind (分別心) with seeing objects as existing (見有境界), and names that ignorance (無明). It is cited only for this explicit equation.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, unable to separate and set out an account. The phrase occurs 100 times in 63 allowlisted texts. It appears both as self-report and as an interview verdict: a monk says he cannot account for a distinction between expounding teachings and responding to the occasion; a master tells a questioner, 'look at you, unable to account for it'; and masters themselves say they cannot account for a fan-name test, a north-or-south salutation, or which recorded saying is deep or shallow. Zhaozhou's 'the highest way is not difficult' exchange supplies a famous duration formula: he says someone once asked him and he was unable to account for it for five years. A later address turns the verb back on the listener: if unable to account for it, one must carefully account for it.
Senses.Note: The Zen deviation lies in public interview: ordinary inability to explain becomes both the participant's admission and the examiner's verdict, while masters also use it of their own inability. 'Explain,' 'distinguish,' and 'sort out' are contextual English renderings of the same act of furnishing an account, not different things; the corpus does not warrant multiple senses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問：至道無難，唯嫌揀擇。是時人窠臼否？師曰：曾有人問我，老僧直得五年分疏不下。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Zhaozhou's exchange supplies the fixed five-year formula.

Occurrences.Kwic: 云：王爺還是演教？還是酬機？王云：先演教，後酬機。云：衲子分疏不下。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A monk explicitly reports inability to account for the distinction made in a public exchange.

Senses.Explanation: A coordinate pair naming “principle” and “affairs, events, or matters.” Chan records ask how principle and affairs are unobstructed, say that both sides have been penetrated or are fully provided, and require them to be clearly distinguished. The Mirror Record gives one explicit account of their relation: “This principle is the principle that completes affairs; this affair is the affair that displays principle.” Ying’an says, “Penetrated on the side of principle and penetrated on the side of affairs: this is called principle and affairs fused through.” Other records speak of both being complete or ask directly, “What are principle and affairs?” The expression is translated as the coordinate pair stated by the texts rather than collapsed into one abstract category.
Senses.Note: The corpus has 850 matches in 198 files. Recurrent constructions include 'principle and affairs unobstructed' (117 matches in 63 files), 'principle and affairs perfectly fused' (24 in 21), 'principle and affairs both complete' (11 in 9), and 'principle and affairs distinct and clear' (9 in 6). Forty-six occurrences in thirty files ask, 'What are principle and affairs?' or use that wording within a fuller question. These distributions support one corpus-wide sense rather than a master-specific one.

Occurrences.Kwic: 或理事相即亦得。此理是成事之理。此事是顯理之事。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Mirror Record says that principle and affairs may be mutually identical: this principle is the principle that completes affairs, and this affair is the affair that displays principle.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如何是理事無礙法界？師曰：東西南北。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A question asks, 'What is the realm in which principle and affairs are unobstructed?' The teacher answers, 'East, west, south, north.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 理上也透，事上也透，所謂理事融徹
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Ying'an says, 'Penetrated on the side of principle and penetrated on the side of affairs: this is what is called principle and affairs fused through.'
A record says, 'Whether proclaimed aloud or shown silently, principle and affairs are both complete.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 今宗鏡本意。要理事分明。方顯一心體用具足。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Mirror Record says its basic intention requires principle and affairs to be distinct and clear; only then does it display the substance and function of one mind as fully present.
